papers.title: OmniOpt: Taxonomy, Geometry, and Benchmarking of Modern Optimizers

summary.tldr: OmniOpt introduces a unified survey and benchmark for over one hundred optimizers, using a five-stage meta-pipeline and norm-constrained linear minimization oracles to create a dual-dimension taxonomy and cross-domain benchmark.
key_points: OmniOpt models optimizer updates as structured transformations through a five-stage meta-pipeline, noting most methods utilize only one or two stages.
Norm-constrained linear minimization oracles (LMOs) are used to unify different optimizers conceptually.
A dual-dimension taxonomy categorizes optimizers by mechanism family and measurable training objectives.
The taxonomy is instantiated in a cross-domain benchmark covering language model pretraining and image classification, analyzing optimizer families across multiple effect objectives.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a systematic framework for selecting optimizers based on explicit mechanism and objective assumptions, guiding future optimizer development.

papers.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Continual GUI Agent Learning

summary.tldr: UI-MOPD introduces multi-teacher on-policy distillation for continual learning in GUI agents, addressing challenges in cross-platform interaction by balancing capability retention and new-platform adaptation.
key_points: Constructed Uni-GUI, a high-quality cross-platform GUI interaction dataset to address data scarcity and limited platform coverage.
Proposed UI-MOPD, the first method incorporating multi-teacher on-policy distillation into continual learning for GUI agents.
UI-MOPD dynamically selects a platform-specific teacher and transfers behavioral priors to a shared policy via platform-conditioned distillation.
Achieved task success rates of 38.2% on OSWorld and 12.0% on MobileWorld, demonstrating effectiveness in balancing cross-platform capability retention and new-platform adaptation.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables GUI agents to adapt to new platforms while preserving existing capabilities, crucial for developing robust cross-platform interaction systems.

papers.title: PixWorld: Unifying 3D Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Pixel Space

summary.tldr: PixWorld unifies 3D scene generation and reconstruction in pixel space using a single diffusion model, directly supervising on rendered images to improve fidelity and overcome latent-space limitations.
key_points: PixWorld unifies 3D reconstruction and generation within a pixel-space diffusion paradigm, eliminating the need for separate models.
The model directly supervises diffusion on rendered images, avoiding information loss from latent encoding and pretrained VAE/RAE dependencies.
A geometry perception loss is introduced, aligning rendered views with ground truth in a 3D foundation model's geometry-aware feature space for structural supervision.
PixWorld outperforms prior latent-space generation methods and matches state-of-the-art reconstruction methods.
summary.why_it_matters: This unified pixel-space approach simplifies 3D scene processing pipelines and improves the fidelity of both generated and reconstructed 3D content.

papers.title: ResearchStudio-Reel: Automate the Last Mile of Research from Paper to Poster, Video, and Blog

summary.tldr: ResearchStudio-Reel automates research dissemination into editable posters, videos, and blogs using a shared extractor and deterministic primitives, outperforming prior systems.
key_points: ResearchStudio-Reel uses five Claude Code and Codex skills: one shared extractor (Paper2Assets), three editable generators (Paper2Poster, Paper2Video, Paper2Blog), and one interactive convergence layer (Paper2Reel).
Paper2Assets extracts paper content once into a shared bundle for reuse by all downstream skills.
The system generates print-ready posters, synchronized talk videos, and bilingual blogs that maintain factual consistency and are round-trip editable in PowerPoint or Word.
On the Paper2Poster benchmark, ResearchStudio-Reel posters surpassed prior automated systems and frontier LLMs in aesthetic and information criteria, winning 84-93% of papers.
ResearchStudio-Reel uniquely pairs narration-aligned on-slide highlights with a bilingual blog gated by layout-aware DOCX repair, enabling all three editable artifacts.
summary.why_it_matters: This system streamlines the labor-intensive process of converting research papers into various dissemination formats, improving efficiency and consistency.

papers.title: ResearchStudio-Idea: An Evidence-Grounded Research-Ideation Skill Suite from ML Conference Outcomes

summary.tldr: ResearchStudio-Idea is a skill suite for evidence-grounded research ideation, including Paper-Search, Scoop-Check, and IdeaSpark, which uses 15 ideation patterns derived from 1,947 ML conference papers to generate stronger research proposals.
key_points: ResearchStudio-Idea comprises Paper-Search (multi-source literature search), Scoop-Check (prior-art collision checker), and IdeaSpark (end-to-end ideation workflow).
IdeaSpark is built from a corpus of 1,947 machine learning conference papers (ICLR, ICML, NeurIPS 2021-2025), including Oral papers, high-citation subsets, and rejected submissions.
Analysis of the corpus identified 31 recurring ideation sub-patterns, consolidated into 15 reusable ideation patterns, each operationalized as a structured card.

IdeaSpark's workflow involves evidence evaluation, context reconstruction, bottleneck identification, pattern selection, candidate direction instantiation, prior work retrieval, and outcome-informed auditing.
Automated-judge evaluations indicate IdeaSpark produces stronger research proposals than no-skill and generic-skill baselines while maintaining competitive novelty.
summary.why_it_matters: This tool suite provides a structured, evidence-based approach to research ideation, potentially improving the quality and novelty of early-stage research proposals.

papers.title: MANCE: Manifold Aware Concept Erasure

summary.tldr: MANCE introduces a Manifold Constraint Hypothesis for concept erasure, projecting concept removal updates onto an estimated manifold to better preserve other information in representations.
key_points: MANCE iteratively updates representations using a classifier's signals, projecting these updates onto a manifold estimated from natural inputs.
Evaluated across 119 settings, including 13 language models, three NLP concepts, and 40 CelebA-CLIP attributes, MANCE consistently improved leakage results when applied with previous methods.
MANCE+ and MANCE++ prepend a closed-form erasure algorithm to MANCE, achieving improved leakage-surgicality tradeoffs.
MANCE++ achieves state-of-the-art results in nonlinear concept erasure.
summary.why_it_matters: This method offers a more effective way to remove specific concepts from AI model representations while minimizing damage to other encoded information.

papers.title: Bridging Interleaved Multi-Modal Reasoning as a Unified Decision Process

summary.tldr: BRAID unifies multi-turn text-image-text reasoning as a single Markov Decision Process, enabling joint reinforcement learning optimization of both textual and visual generation, addressing limitations of prior text-only RL approaches.
key_points: BRAID casts multi-turn text-image-text reasoning as a unified Markov Decision Process (MDP) for joint optimization.
It computes a shared trajectory-level advantage, propagating it to both text tokens and image denoising paths.
Modality-native policy gradient mechanisms are used for optimizing text and image generation.
A vision-language model (VLM) judge provides dense turn-level feedback by scoring intermediate images for reasoning utility.
summary.why_it_matters: This unified RL approach improves multi-modal reasoning performance on spatial reasoning and visual perception benchmarks.

papers.title: Wan-Streamer v0.2: Higher Resolution, Same Latency

summary.tldr: Wan-Streamer v0.2 increases interactive output stream resolution from 192x336 to 640x368 while maintaining approximately 200 ms model-side latency and supporting scene-grounded mid-shot agents.
key_points: Output resolution increased from 192x336 to 640x368 at 25 FPS.
Model-side signal-to-signal latency remains approximately 200 ms.
Thinker component remains a single-GPU low-latency path for streaming perception and language/state Transformer pass.
Performer component uses a multi-GPU Ulysses-style context-parallel group for next-unit latent generation, sharding long visual sequences across ranks for denoising.
Total remote interaction latency is approximately 550 ms, including a 350 ms bidirectional network budget.
summary.why_it_matters: The higher resolution allows for more detailed and legible real-time interaction with virtual agents, improving realism and utility.

papers.title: GigaWorld-1: A Roadmap to Build World Models for Robot Policy Evaluation

summary.tldr: This work introduces WMBench, a benchmark for robotic policy evaluation using world models, and GigaWorld-1, a world model optimized for this task, based on analyzing 7 video world models and 4 action representations.
key_points: WMBench is a benchmark constructed from real-robot teleoperation data and matched policy rollouts covering diverse manipulation tasks.
Evaluator quality is dominated by long-horizon, action-faithful rollout consistency, not short-term visual realism.
Pretraining gains require balancing general world knowledge with robot-specific controllability.
Architectural choices (action encoding, memory design, evaluator-focused post-training) strongly determine alignment with real-world robot behavior.
GigaWorld-1 is a world model specifically optimized for policy evaluation, developed from these insights.
summary.why_it_matters: This research provides a roadmap and tools to enable scalable and reliable evaluation of embodied robot foundation models, reducing reliance on costly real-world rollouts.

papers.title: Multi-Turn Agentic Scientific Literature Search via Workflow Induction

summary.tldr: PaperPilot introduces a multi-turn literature search agent that frames scientific search as workflow induction, allowing explicit control and refinement of search strategies through an executable DAG of operators.
key_points: PaperPilot constructs an executable Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of paper-search operators (e.g., keyword search, citation expansion, filtering, scoring, reranking, evidence extraction) based on an anchor paper and user query.
User feedback refines both the query and the search workflow itself, addressing underspecified and evolving user intents.
PaperPilot is trained using supervised workflow imitation and preference optimization over controlled workflow corruptions.

PaperPilot-9B improves Hit@5 from 58.0 to 77.0, MRR from 47.5 to 59.4, and nDCG@10 from 26.8 to 32.5 compared to the base Qwen3.5-9B toolset agent, while reducing workflow execution errors from 9.5% to 0%.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach provides a more controllable and effective interface for aligning literature search agents with complex scientific intent, improving search accuracy and reducing errors.

papers.title: Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders

summary.tldr: A 5-billion-parameter latent diffusion model is introduced, capable of generating real-time, multi-player Rocket League matches by conditioning on multiple agents' action streams, maintaining coherence and stability for extended durations.
key_points: The model is the first multiplayer world model, conditioning on action streams of multiple agents to attribute scene changes and maintain coherence under arbitrary action combinations.
Trained on 10,000 hours of Rocket League gameplay, the 5-billion-parameter latent diffusion model generates four-player matches at 20 frames per second on a single Nvidia B200 GPU.
Rollouts maintain distributional quality for at least five minutes, and in practice continue for hours without collapse, despite training only on short clips.
The research systematically investigates video codec, generative objective, and multiplayer conditioning scheme, and includes targeted evaluations of physical understanding.
summary.why_it_matters: This work enables more realistic and interactive simulations for complex multi-agent environments, potentially advancing AI training and virtual world development.

papers.title: InternVLA-A1.5: Unifying Understanding, Latent Foresight, and Action for Compositional Generalization

summary.tldr: InternVLA-A1.5 unifies VLM semantics, latent foresight, and action for robot manipulation by leveraging a native VLM backbone and a latent-querying future prediction mechanism supervised by a frozen video generation model.
key_points: InternVLA-A1.5 builds its policy on a native VLM backbone, maintaining VQA and subtask prediction capabilities.
Future prediction is reframed as a latent-querying problem, using learnable foresight tokens to condense task-relevant future information.
A frozen pretrained video generation model supervises the latent-querying process, allowing the policy to inherit world-model dynamics priors without pixel-level generation.
The video branch is discarded during inference to enable real-time control.
InternVLA-A1.5 was pretrained on 1.2M robot episodes and 3M multimodal samples, achieving top results on six simulation benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach improves robot compositional generalization and long-horizon execution by preserving VLM semantics and integrating dynamics priors efficiently.

papers.title: EVA-Client: A Unified Data Collection, Inference, and Deployment Framework for Embodied Policies on Real Robots

summary.tldr: EVA-Client is an open-source framework unifying data collection, inference, and deployment for embodied manipulation policies on real robots, featuring a decoupled architecture and integrated evaluation-as-data-collection.
key_points: Features a component-decoupled architecture where robot backends, inference strategies, and transport middlewares are orthogonal, allowing independent additions.
Provides inspectable execution via Debug, Collect, and Eval workflows, supporting modes from open-loop simulation to continuous real-time control.
Every evaluation run automatically collects full rollouts in a training-ready format, including logs and side-by-side comparison, to feed subsequent training rounds.
Consolidates major real-time inference strategies, including synchronous/asynchronous execution, ACT-style temporal ensembling, and Real-Time Chunking, under a single configuration.
summary.why_it_matters: This framework streamlines the policy iteration loop for real-robot manipulation, accelerating development and improving data efficiency.

papers.title: KVpop -- Key-Value Cache Compression with Predictive Online Pruning

summary.tldr: KVpop introduces a learned, fixed-budget KV eviction policy for autoregressive decoding, directly supervising keep-or-drop decisions against a novel future-attention target to achieve significant KV cache compression.
key_points: KVpop learns a fixed-budget KV eviction policy by directly supervising the keep-or-drop decision for cache entries.
The eviction scorer is trained against a novel future-attention target, computed efficiently without materializing dense attention maps.
A delayed memory-based scorer defers scoring for a fixed number of steps to exploit near-future context, a unique feature among learned eviction methods.
On Qwen3-4B, KVpop retains 98% of full-attention performance at 75% KV cache compression and 97% at 88% compression on AIME and HMMT mathematical reasoning tasks.
Qwen3-8B shows near-full teacher performance, outperforming established eviction baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly reduces memory and bandwidth costs in autoregressive decoding by compressing the KV cache while maintaining model performance.

papers.title: Do All Visual Tokens Matter Equally? Object-Evidence Preserving Token Merging for Vision-Language Retrieval

summary.tldr: SaMer is an object-aware token merging framework that compresses image-side post-projector tokens into K representative centroids, preserving object evidence for vision-language retrieval.
key_points: SaMer compresses image-side post-projector tokens into K representative centroids while maintaining the original late-interaction interface.
Object annotations are used only during training as a merge prior to prevent cross-instance mixing, with no bounding boxes or detectors required at inference.
With K=64, SaMer removes over 93% of image-side tokens and reduces ColPali storage by 16.09 times.
SaMer improves R@1 on Flickr30K and MSCOCO, outperforming compression baselines and showing stronger phrase-level grounding.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly reduces storage and scoring costs for multi-vector vision-language retrieval while improving performance by preserving critical object evidence.

papers.title: Do Modules Stay in Their Lane? Role Drift in Compound LLM Systems

summary.tldr: This paper introduces "Role Drift," a failure mode in compound LLM systems where modules deviate from assigned roles despite maintaining end-task performance, and proposes "Role Anchor" to mitigate it.
key_points: Role Drift occurs when modules in compound LLM systems achieve high end-task accuracy by violating their assigned roles, e.g., a decomposer planting answers or a reader using parametric memory instead of retrieved passages.

Role Anchor is a regularizer designed to make role drift observable and controllable during end-to-end training by preserving how a role prompt shifts a module's next-token predictions relative to a neutral prompt.

Experiments show that for a decomposer pipeline, 86% of apparent reinforcement learning gain vanished when the decomposer was constrained to its role, indicating accuracy alone can overstate learning.
Role Anchor mitigates role drift across two pipelines with a tunable accuracy cost, and gradient analysis suggests it reduces alignment with the role-drift direction.
summary.why_it_matters: Detecting and mitigating role drift is crucial for understanding true system learning and ensuring modules perform their intended functions in compound LLM architectures.

papers.title: Reliability-Aware LLM Alignment from Inconsistent Human Feedback

summary.tldr: RGPO is a new framework that improves LLM alignment by estimating annotator reliability and dynamically modulating training based on annotation consensus, addressing human feedback inconsistency.
key_points: Existing preference optimization frameworks like DPO treat ambiguous and unanimous human feedback identically, leading to overfitting on inconsistent supervision.
RGPO estimates annotator reliability and infers latent ground truth labels from noisy human feedback to identify robust preferences.
RGPO introduces a reliability-aware consistency optimization that dynamically modulates the training objective based on the consensus level of annotations.
Experiments on LLM alignment benchmarks show RGPO reduces inconsistency and noise, outperforming widely adopted RLHF baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves LLM alignment by making RLHF more robust to the inherent inconsistencies and subjectivity of human feedback.

papers.title: When Does In-Context Search Help? A Sampling-Complexity Theory of Reflection-Driven Reasoning

summary.tldr: A theoretical analysis models in-context search as approximate inference, showing exponential improvements in success probability when reflections localize early mistakes, and demonstrating robustness and learnability of these gains.
key_points: In-context search is modeled as approximate inference over reasoning traces, with the base model defining a prior and self-reflection providing feedback for posterior updates.

When reflections reliably localize early mistakes, in-context search yields exponential improvements over the base model, solving problems with exponentially small zero-shot pass rates using polynomial sequential attempts.
If reflections fail to localize mistakes, conditioning on past attempts offers no asymptotic benefit over parallel sampling.
Approximate posterior updates suffice, and cross-entropy training on search rollouts recovers the required behavior with polynomial sample complexity.
Under a stagewise abstraction of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, the optimal policy extension implements the same posterior reweighting rule.
summary.why_it_matters: This theory explains the effectiveness of in-context search in LLMs and provides guidance for its robust implementation and training.

papers.title: When Should LLMs Search? Counterfactual Supervision for Search Routing

summary.tldr: This paper introduces counterfactual supervision for search routing in LLMs, improving macro-F1 from 0.7082 to 0.8235 for Gemma E2B and 0.7053 to 0.8365 for Qwen3.5-4B.
key_points: The problem is framed as an instance-level search-routing decision: whether search is needed to improve task success relative to a no-search execution.
An oracle is constructed using no-search and forced-search outcomes, classifying instances as NO SEARCH, SEARCH, or UNSOLVED based on task-specific success.
Search-routing policies were trained using supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization.
Routing macro-F1 on oracle-eligible examples improved from 0.7082 to 0.8235 for Gemma E2B and from 0.7053 to 0.8365 for Qwen3.5-4B.
Gemma E2B primarily learned no-search restraint, while Qwen3.5-4B further reduced missed search.
summary.why_it_matters: Improved search routing can optimize resource use and enhance the reliability of search-augmented language models by reducing unnecessary searches and improving evidence utilization.

papers.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion: A Tri-Mode Language Model Unifying Autoregressive, Diffusion, and Self-Speculation Decoding

summary.tldr: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion is a tri-mode language model unifying autoregressive, diffusion, and self-speculation decoding, trained with a joint AR-diffusion objective for high throughput.
key_points: The model combines AR and diffusion objectives, where diffusion improves lookahead planning and AR provides left-to-right linguistic priors.
In self-speculation mode, diffusion drafts and AR verifies, outperforming multi-token prediction (MTP) methods in acceptance rate and real-device efficiency.
Diffusion shows potential for 76.5% more tokens per forward pass than self-speculation under an optimal sampler.
Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-8B decodes 6x more tokens per forward than Qwen3-8B with comparable accuracy, achieving 4x higher throughput on SPEED-Bench with SGLang on a GB200 GPU.
summary.why_it_matters: This model family offers significant improvements in both accuracy and speed for language models across various deployment settings and concurrency levels.

papers.title: SpanUQ: Span-Level Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Model Generation

summary.tldr: SpanUQ introduces Span-Level Uncertainty Estimation (SLUE) for LLMs, using a lightweight probe with a DETR-style span decoder and Mixture of Beta distribution to quantify uncertainty in semantically coherent text spans.
key_points: SpanUQ formalizes Span-Level Uncertainty Estimation (SLUE) to address limitations of token-level and sequence-level uncertainty methods.
The SPANUQ probe distills multi-sample inference uncertainty into a single forward pass over LLM hidden states.
SPANUQ employs a DETR-style span decoder to detect spans and estimate uncertainty via a Mixture of Beta distribution, trained with Beta NLL regression and contrastive ranking.
SPANUQ-BENCH, a benchmark of 20K prompts and 293K annotated spans with continuous soft labels, was created for span-level uncertainty evaluation.
SPANUQ achieves 0.910 F1 for span detection, outperforming heuristic baselines by 39.4%, and is 10-20x faster than sampling-based methods.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more granular and efficient way to localize and quantify uncertainty in LLM outputs, improving trustworthiness and enabling self-refinement.

papers.title: Auditing of Unlearning Algorithms

summary.tldr: A new auditor uses membership inference attacks to compute data-dependent lower bounds on the unlearning parameter ε, differentiating between rigorously guaranteed and empirical unlearning algorithms.
key_points: The proposed auditor computes data-dependent lower bounds on the unlearning parameter ε using membership inference attacks.
Algorithms with rigorous guarantees (model clipping, rewind-to-delete) achieve very small ε bounds, consistent with their unlearning claims.
Empirical methods (Hessian-based unlearning, interleaved ascent-descent, ascent on the forget set, fine-tuning on the retain set) exhibit large ε bounds, indicating poor unlearning.
The auditor provides a practical tool for empirically falsifying unlearning claims via a hypothesis-testing framework.
Validation was performed on CIFAR-100 and Shakespeare text datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: This auditor offers a practical method to empirically assess the effectiveness of machine unlearning algorithms, ensuring data privacy and compliance.

papers.title: Beyond Refusal: A Same-Lineage Study of Aligned and Abliterated LLMs for Vulnerability Analysis

summary.tldr: This study compares aligned and refusal-ablated LLMs from the same lineage (Gemma, Qwen) to isolate the effect of safety state on vulnerability analysis tasks, finding ablated models often perform better.
key_points: The study compares Aligned (refusal behavior intact) and Abliterated (refusal-ablated) same-lineage LLMs (Gemma, Qwen) to assess safety state impact on defensive utility in software security.

In a Gemma-based Java/Vul4J repair-validation study, Abliterated models achieved higher patch usability (67.8% vs. 29.9%), successful application (65.0% vs. 24.9%), and successful compilation (32.8% vs. 9.0%) compared to Aligned models.
For Qwen models, Abliterated improved localization performance, increasing line-level F1 from 2.08% to 3.91% and Top-1 accuracy from 4.10% to 6.95%.
Evaluations included vulnerability detection, CWE attribution, vulnerable-line localization, root-cause localization, and executable patch validation, with prompt wording as a controlled variable.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how LLM safety states affect defensive utility is crucial for developing effective and actionable LLM-based security assistants.

papers.title: REFORGE: A Method for Benchmarking LLMs' Reverse Engineering Capabilities in Decompiled Binary Function Naming

summary.tldr: Reforge is a new provenance-tracked pipeline for benchmarking LLMs' reverse engineering capabilities in decompiled binary function naming, addressing ground truth reliability under compiler optimization.
key_points: Reforge constructs function-level ground truth from C source through compilation, DWARF and syntactic extraction, alignment, and decompilation.
It operationalizes alignment uncertainty with an eight-gate confidence funnel and three-tier stratification.
On a micro-benchmark, high-confidence yield decreased from 87.2% to 65.9% across optimization levels.
Unpaired comparisons overstate optimization-induced performance decay due to survivorship bias.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables more reliable and uncertainty-aware benchmarking of LLMs in reverse engineering tasks, particularly for binary analysis.

papers.title: Scaling Closed-Loop Feature Channel Configuration with LLMs

summary.tldr: Scaling closed-loop LLM-based channel configuration search to 250 candidates per cycle confirmed optimization behavior, improved accuracy, and revealed architectural regularities, including parameter efficiency and non-power-of-two widths.
key_points: The search scaled to 250 candidate networks per fine-tuning cycle, evaluating 462 verified CIFAR-100 candidates from 8 cycles and 2000 generated candidates.
Per-cycle mean accuracy showed a positive linear trend with a slope of 9.87e-4 (p=0.043), and the best observed accuracy increased from 0.3144 to 0.3676.
The best model achieved 0.3676 accuracy with 11.8M parameters, demonstrating improved parameter efficiency compared to an earlier model at 0.3144 with 166.5M parameters.

Non-power-of-two channel widths were present in 41.8% of verified candidates, and strong models exhibited structured channel-allocation patterns with moderate early widths and expanded middle/later blocks.
summary.why_it_matters: This demonstrates that LLM-driven neural architecture search can effectively optimize network parameters and discover efficient, novel architectures at scale.

vendors.title: Expanding Managed Agents in Gemini API: background tasks, remote MCP and more

summary.tldr: New capabilities for Managed Agents in Gemini API are announced, enabling developers to build reliable, production-ready agents.
key_points: New capabilities are being introduced for Managed Agents in Gemini API.
These capabilities aim to support the development of reliable agents.
The enhancements are designed for building production-ready agents.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can now create more robust and deployable agents using the Gemini API.
